newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia sets car talks with trade giants.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia sets car talks with trade giants.

text.p: Indonesia's trade and industry minister said on Friday Jakarta had scheduled talks with Japan, the United States and the European Union (EU) on its controversial national car policy.
"We will talk with Japan, the United States and Europe bilaterally starting early next month," Tunky Ariwibowo told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
"As I said before, we will try to settle (the car issue) outside the WTO (World Trade Organisation)," he said.
He said the venues and the dates for the talks have not been set.

Indonesia's national car policy gives PT Timor Putra Nasional, a company controlled by Suharto's youngest son, Hutomo Mandala Putra tax and tariff breaks to produce a national car in association with Kia Motors Corp of South Korea.
Japan, the United States and the EU have said the policy discriminates against other manufacturers and have brought their complaint to the WTO.
Indonesia has said the national car programme is aimed at strenthening its domestic industry.
Indonesia last week blocked a request by the EU to set up a dispute settlement panel to look into whether Jakarta's national car project was in violation of international trade regulations.
